newsitem.title: INDIA: India to tune trade rules in line with WTO.
newsitem.headline: India to tune trade rules in line with WTO.

text.p: India will continue to modify its trade norms in line with recommendations of the World Trade Organisation (WTO), a senior Commerce Ministry official said on Wednesday.
"We are looking forward to improve our trade. The government is trying to make trade free as recommended under the WTO" said Shyamal Ghosh, India's highest ranking foreign trade official.
India signed the WTO accord in 1994 and has a 10-year transitional period until 2005 in which to strengthen its intellectual property rights legislation in line with the accord.
Ghosh was addressing a traders' meet on boosting trade with the Commonwealth of Independent of States (CIS) in New Delhi.
He said Indian authorities would start imposing stringent measures against traders exporting poor quality goods.
"The Directorate General of Foreign Trade would take action against those who export substandard goods and engage in other malpractices", Ghosh said
Indian exports in the year are expected to increase 19.5 percent to $38 billion in 1996/97 from $31.8 in 1995/96.
Ghosh also reiterated India's need to improve the land route to the CIS to expand trade ties with the former Soviet republics.
"We would like to smoothen the land route for trade purposes via Iran as the sea route to most of the CIS countries is circular, lengthier and much more expensive," he said.
Analysts forecast India's trade with CIS to rise to $5 billion by 2000, with completion of a missing rail link in Iran.
India's trade with the former Soviet republics fell almost 88 percent in 1992/93 (April-March) from levels in 1990/91, after the disintegration of the Soviet Union.
Bilateral trade between India and CIS in 1995/96 stood at 77.08 billion rupees ($ 2.16 billion). Russia accounted for about 70 percent of imports and 92 percent of exports to the CIS, officials said.
Ghosh said India's two largest trading firms, the State Trading Corporation and MMTC Ltd, to set up warehouses in Russia. He said there were plans for more Indian warehouses in other CIS countries.
During the last five years some 77 Indo-CIS joint collaborations in power, cargo services and textiles sectors have been approved by India.
